title: Sysmon Executable or Script Creation in Selected User-Writable Paths
exclusions: Reports Sysmon FileCreate Event ID 11 when an executable or script extension is created or overwritten under the locally selected Windows Temp, per-user AppData Temp, Startup, or ProgramData path classes. Event 11 proves a file operation by the recorded process; path and extension alone do not prove execution, persistence, malware, successful write contents, signer, hash, file prevalence, or user intent. The rule excludes other paths and extensions, file renames/deletes, alternate data streams, registry persistence, and hosts where Sysmon FileCreate is not enabled. Its path list, 15-minute closed interval, five-minute arrival delay, and notification policy are deployment choices. Missing hosts, duplicate direct/WEF collection, path aliases, junctions, short names, environment-variable expansion, and incomplete fields are source-health or normalization limits. This UC does not quarantine files, kill processes, or attest endpoint protection.
evidence: Retain the version-controlled `windows_sysmon_selected_path_file_create` search, schedule, ACL, result history, exact path/extension policy and exception approvals; every result with destination, EventRecordID, UTC event time, Image, ProcessGuid/ProcessId, TargetFilename, User, RuleName, source metadata and index time; raw Event 11 XML; effective Sysmon binary/config/schema version and FileCreate filters; expected-host and duplicate-route health; asset, signer/hash/prevalence, process-tree and change context; alert delivery and analyst disposition; and dated positive, negative, boundary, duplicate, delay, field-loss, upgrade and exception tests. This documentation-only review created no Sysmon event, SPL dispatch, file, alert, containment action, or runtime evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index and fixed closed interval, ingest one XML Event 11 from provider `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon` with destination `ws-lab-01`, unique EventRecordID `66001`, Image `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`, ProcessGuid `{11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111}`, User `EXAMPLE\analyst`, and TargetFilename `C:\Users\analyst\AppData\Local\Temp\uc-1.2.66.ps1`. Expect exactly one row classified `user_temp`, extension `ps1`, preserving all named fields. Repeat independently with an `.exe` under the all-users Startup path and expect `startup`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for each isolated variant: EventCode other than 11; provider mismatch; missing destination, EventRecordID, Image, or TargetFilename; `.txt` in the selected Temp path; `.exe` under `C:\Windows\System32`; `.exe` whose directory merely contains the word `Temporary`; a FileDelete event; wrong source/source type; an event in the newest excluded five minutes; and two copies of the same destination/EventRecordID. Verify case-insensitive path/extension matching and slash normalization. Duplicate and missing-host health must still report.

dataSources: Microsoft Sysinternals Sysmon Operational Event ID 11 (`FileCreate`) from `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, generated only where the installed Sysmon configuration includes the operation. Collect XML with Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709) or a validated Splunk Windows Event Log input to deployment-choice `index=wineventlog`, exact `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`. Required fields: `_time, _indextime, Computer|dest|host, EventCode|EventID, Provider_Name|ProviderName, EventRecordID|RecordNumber, UtcTime, Image, ProcessGuid, ProcessId, TargetFilename, User`; preserve RuleName. Sysmon configuration, event manifest, and raw XML are authoritative for field/version behavior.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (`Splunk_TA_microsoft_sysmon`, Splunkbase 5709) for Sysmon collection/CIM knowledge; a restricted local content app owns the raw analytic, source health, dashboard, fixtures, and `windows_sysmon_file_create_exceptions.csv`.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=11 earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval event_id=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), provider=lower(trim(coalesce(Provider_Name,ProviderName))), destination=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,dest,host))), event_record_id=trim(tostring(coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber))), image=lower(replace(trim(Image),"/","\\")), target_filename=lower(replace(trim(TargetFilename),"/","\\"))
| eval extension=lower(replace(target_filename,"^.*\.",""))
| eval path_class=case(match(target_filename,"^.:\\users\\[^\\]+\\appdata\\local\\temp\\"),"user_temp",match(target_filename,"^.:\\windows\\temp\\"),"windows_temp",match(target_filename,"\\start menu\\programs\\startup\\"),"startup",match(target_filename,"^.:\\programdata\\"),"programdata")
| where event_id=11 AND provider="microsoft-windows-sysmon" AND len(destination)>0 AND len(event_record_id)>0 AND len(image)>0 AND len(target_filename)>0 AND isnotnull(path_class) AND in(extension,"exe","dll","ps1","bat","cmd","vbs","js","jse","hta","scr")
| stats count AS duplicate_count min(_time) AS event_time max(_indextime) AS last_indextime values(UtcTime) AS sysmon_utc values(ProcessGuid) AS process_guids values(ProcessId) AS process_ids values(User) AS users values(RuleName) AS rule_names values(source) AS observed_sources values(sourcetype) AS observed_sourcetypes by destination event_record_id image target_filename path_class extension
| where duplicate_count=1
| eval aggregation_window_minutes=15, close_delay_minutes=5, analytic_interpretation="selected-path file create or overwrite; investigate context; path and extension do not prove malware, execution, or persistence", use_case="UC-1.2.66"
| table event_time destination event_record_id image process_guids process_ids target_filename path_class extension users rule_names sysmon_utc observed_sources observed_sourcetypes last_indextime aggregation_window_minutes close_delay_minutes analytic_interpretation use_case
| sort 0 -event_time destination target_filename
description: Reports one destination/EventRecordID row for each unique Sysmon Event 11 in a closed 15-minute interval whose normalized target has a selected executable/script extension and falls under the configured Temp, Startup, or ProgramData path classes. The row preserves creator-process and file context; it is a triage lead, not a malware verdict.
value: Focused file-creation telemetry can expose payload staging, persistence preparation, administrative tooling, packaging, or software-delivery activity early enough to correlate the creating process and file reputation. Explicit path and extension scope makes volume and tuning measurable while avoiding the unsupported claim that every write in a user-writable directory is malicious.
implementation: Deploy and inventory a supported Sysmon build/configuration, enable Event 11 only with a reviewed volume policy, and collect the Operational channel as XML. Validate provider, original destination, record identity, Image, TargetFilename and ProcessGuid before saving `windows_sysmon_selected_path_file_create`. Run every 15 minutes over the delayed closed slice, alert on any row, and investigate process ancestry, file hash/signature/prevalence, execution and change context before response.
visualization: Restricted `Windows — Selected-Path File Creation` dashboard: expected-host/config and duplicate-route health first; counts by path class, extension, creator Image and destination; event timeline; and a result table matching the SPL. Drill down to raw Event 11, Sysmon Event 1 process tree, Event 15/23/26 where collected, file hash/signature/prevalence, endpoint detections, user/session, asset criticality and approved deployment/change records. Label all panels “file creation/overwrite—not execution or malware proof.”
schema: Sysmon FileCreate Event ID 11 native XML fields
dataModelAcceleration: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon maps supported events into Endpoint, but accelerated Filesystem field names and event identity must be verified against the installed add-on/CIM versions. The raw rule requires native Event 11 provider, Image, ProcessGuid, TargetFilename, RuleName and EventRecordID uniqueness. No `cimSpl` is claimed until a local parity test proves the same path, extension, closed-window and duplicate semantics.

knownFalsePositives:
A result should represent a real Event 11 file create/overwrite. Benign causes include:

1. **Configuration Manager, Intune, PDQ, winget, Chocolatey, enterprise installer or patcher** — packages stage executables/scripts under Temp or ProgramData. Match deployment ID, package hash/signature, creator process/parent, account, destination collection, UTC bounds and success.
2. **Browser, Office, archive utility or updater** — downloads/extractions use per-user Temp before moving files. Correlate URL/Zone.Identifier, browser process tree, signer/hash, destination, user action and later execution.
3. **PowerShell, CI/CD, developer build or test harness** — approved scripts and compiled artifacts can land in Temp. Require repository/job/run ID, runner identity, source commit, expected filename/hash and timebox.
4. **Security scanner, EDR or sandbox** — products may create canary or test artifacts. Verify product console action, binary signer, rule/test ID, source process and cleanup.
5. **Logon script, Group Policy, packaging or profile tool** — Startup and ProgramData writes may be authorized persistence. Confirm GPO/package, owner, exact destination set, content hash and approved change.
6. **Sysmon configuration change or duplicate collection** — wider FileCreate filters increase volume; direct plus WEF paths duplicate records. Compare config hash/version and repair collection authority.
7. **Authorized purple-team drop** — preserve the result as control evidence and suppress only duplicate delivery within the approved engagement.

**Safe suppression:** apply lookup windows_sysmon_file_create_exceptions.csv only after the base result. Require exact normalized `destination,image,path_class,extension`, optional exact target-prefix/hash constraint, `exception_id`, numeric `valid_from_epoch` and exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket and purpose. Reject wildcard hosts/images, all-Temp exclusions and open-ended dates. Never suppress source/config/duplicate health; retain base events for hunting.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft Sysmon Event 11/configuration guidance and primary Splunk Sysmon/Windows XML documentation; collection, fields, path policy, SPL, fixtures, source health, dashboard, suppression and response were specified but not executed or Microsoft/Sysmon/Splunk/endpoint-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: Event 11 volume depends directly on Sysmon FileCreate filters. The query scans one closed 15-minute slice and aggregates by native record identity; measure event rate and multi-value size before broadening paths or extensions.

detailedImplementation:
## Define and own the signal

Assign Sysmon engineering, Windows endpoint, Splunk collection/content, SOC, incident-response and exception owners. Inventory every host in scope with canonical destination, environment, owner, criticality, Sysmon version, configuration hash, FileCreate include/exclude policy, forwarding route and expected silence. Restrict access because file paths, users and process identifiers can expose sensitive activity.

Microsoft states Event 11 records when a file is created or overwritten. It does not state that the operation executed the file or established persistence. The local policy selects executable/script suffixes under per-user AppData Local Temp, Windows Temp, any Start Menu Programs Startup segment, and root ProgramData. Document this exact list and review it after software-baseline changes. Junctions, aliases, 8.3 names and paths outside those classes can evade literal matching.

## Configure Sysmon and XML collection

Deploy Sysmon from Microsoft Sysinternals with a version-controlled configuration and the Splunk-supported add-on from Splunkbase 5709. Include FileCreate events needed by this rule and estimate volume before broad rollout. Use `sysmon64 -c` and the Operational Event 16 configuration-change record to verify effective configuration; export the schema for the installed version when field behavior is in doubt. Never copy an unreviewed community configuration into production.

Collect `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational` as XML through Splunk Add-on for Sysmon or a tested Windows input. Route to local `wineventlog`; that index name is not a vendor default. Preserve `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, original Computer and EventRecordID. Size channel retention and forwarder queues for outages. During WEF migration, prevent direct and forwarded copies from both being authoritative.

Inspect raw events:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=11 earliest=-30m
| table _time _indextime Computer EventRecordID Provider_Name UtcTime Image ProcessGuid ProcessId TargetFilename User RuleName
| head 50
```

Compare the fields to Event Viewer XML and the installed Sysmon manifest. Verify destination, UTC conversion, process GUID/PID, image, target, user and rule name. A PID can be reused; ProcessGuid plus Event 1 is stronger process correlation. Event 11 does not include file content or a guaranteed hash.

## Maintain source and configuration health

Create an expected-host monitor for absent/stale Sysmon data, excessive `_indextime-_time`, unknown hosts, missing provider/Computer/EventRecordID/Image/TargetFilename, configuration-hash drift, service stop/change events, channel clear/full conditions and duplicate destination/EventRecordID across direct/WEF routes. The analytic rejects duplicate identities rather than allowing duplicate ingest to double pages; health must preserve and route the defect.

Track Event 11 rates by host, Image and RuleName before and after every Sysmon/config/add-on upgrade. An abrupt decrease can mean filtering loss, while an increase can mean a noisy include. Preserve original target paths; do not perform irreversible index-time redaction without a privacy design.

## Schedule and understand the analytic

Save as `windows_sysmon_selected_path_file_create`, run every 15 minutes, and alert when results exceed zero. `earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m` selects a nonoverlapping closed 15-minute event-time slice with five minutes for arrival. Measure p99 forwarding delay and lengthen the delay if required.

The query validates numeric Event 11 and provider, normalizes slash and case, derives the last extension, then assigns one selected path class. It requires destination, record identity, creator Image and target. The first and only aggregation groups destination/EventRecordID and retains forensic fields; `duplicate_count=1` prevents duplicate routes from becoming results. One output row means one qualifying file operation, not one unique file forever. Repeated overwrites with distinct EventRecordIDs remain visible.

## Validate and operationalize

Replay the documented positive fixtures under absolute time bounds and assert every output field. Run each negative separately, including wrong event/provider/source, missing identity, nonselected extension/path, newest delayed events and duplicated records. Test upper/lower case, `/` separators, long paths, Unicode, native and 8.3 names, junction-resolved paths, multiple dots, no extension and boundary timestamps. Confirm duplicate and missing-host health independently.

In an isolated endpoint lab, create a harmless `.ps1` in the selected Temp directory and a signed test executable in an approved Startup test path, then compare raw XML and results. Remove them under the change plan. This proves collection/search behavior only. Measure search runtime, ingest volume, alert delivery, dashboard ACLs, drilldowns and exception expiry before production.

Alert title: `Selected-path file creation on <destination>: <target_filename>`. Analysts verify raw identity and source health, resolve the creating process through Event 1/EDR, inspect parent tree, signer/hash/prevalence and Zone.Identifier, determine whether execution followed, compare deployment/change records, and assess account/asset sensitivity. Escalate only with corroborating evidence. Do not automatically delete/quarantine a file or terminate a process from path alone.

Apply finite exceptions after aggregation and retain the base result. Review path/extension policy, exceptions, source inventory, Sysmon configuration and alert outcomes after every tooling or OS change.

## Troubleshoot

- No Event 11: verify Sysmon service/version, effective FileCreate filter, Operational channel, Windows input, permissions, routing and retention.
- Wrong destination: repair WEF original Computer preservation before searching.
- Missing Image/TargetFilename: compare raw XML, schema version and add-on extraction; do not substitute RenderedDescription silently.
- High volume: identify exact Images/paths and tune Sysmon/configuration or finite alert exceptions; never blanket-exclude Temp.
- Expected file absent: it may be outside selected paths/extensions, created before collection, filtered by Sysmon, renamed rather than created, or represented through an alias.
- CIM differs: audit add-on/CIM version, tags, field aliases, acceleration lag and native event identity; raw XML remains authoritative until parity passes.
grandmaExplanation: We record when Windows programs create certain runnable files in temporary or startup-style folders. Many legitimate installers do this too, so the alert gives investigators the process and path without calling the file malware.
hardware: Windows endpoints and servers running a supported Sysmon build with FileCreate Event 11 configured and the Operational channel collected. Systems without Sysmon, filters that omit selected paths, non-Windows endpoints, network appliances, and products that do not preserve original destination/EventRecordID require separate analytics.
